To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) CIQ, a positive allosteric NMDAR modulator of GluD-containing NMDAR, (ii) increases the activity of striatal cholinergic inter-neurons and (iii) depresses GABAergic transmission through a cholinergically-mediated mechanism, in the striatum (control mice).

CIQ, a positive allosteric NMDAR modulator, increases the firing rate of cholinergic neurons in the intact striatal tissue of control mice, and in the intact dopamine-depleted striatal tissue of the 6-OH-DA-lesioned mouse model, but not in the dopamine-depletd striatum of the 6-0H-DA- lesioned mouse model.

the GluN2B subunit of the N-methyl-d- aspartate receptor (NMDAR) is required for the development of experimental Parkinsonism in a mouse model of the disease, and that the Glu2D subunit of the same receptor has a role in the adaptive changes that occur in the striatum upon loss of dopamine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the modulation of neurotransmission by NMDARs in the basal ganglia of a mouse model for PD.
the identification of the roles and dysfunctions of GluN subunits in experimental Parkinsonism, which may lead to the development of novel therapies for Parkinson's disease.
the modulation of NMDAR subtypes in Parkinson's disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the role of NMDAR subunits is not a simple function of which subunit is present, rather it is a complex function of which subunits are present, the state of their phosphorylation, the state of the synapse they are on, and their interactions with other proteins and other subunits.
the functions of Glu2D containing NMDA receptors in the striatum are changed in the dopamine-deprived striatum, and that the effects of the Glu2D positive allosteric drug are also changed.
the role of Glu N2D containing receptors is not clear and that further studies are required.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GluN2A, GluN2B, and GluN2 D-containing NMDAR subtypes have different functions in different types of striatal neurons.
the positive allosteric modulation of GluN1/GluN2C/GlN2D NMDARs in the striatum is altered in the dopamine-deprived striatum.

the GluN2B-containing NMDAR is responsible for excitatory transmission in both control and Parkinsonian mice, whereas the GluN1/GluN2B-containing receptor is responsible for the inhibitory transmission in control animals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GluN2-containing NMDAR subtypes can be selectively targeted with positive allosteric modulation.
the GluN2-containing NMDA receptors are important modulators of striatal function and that they may be potential targets for therapeutic intervention.
the GluN2-containing NMDAR subtypes have distinct roles in neurotransmission in the intact and dopamine-depleted striata.
